newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul shares end at new 34-month low of 753.34.
newsitem.headline: Seoul shares end at new 34-month low of 753.34.

text.p: South Korean shares declined to provisionally close at a new 34-month low of 753.34 on Wednesday as fears over an economic slowdown and stock oversupply sidelined investors, brokers said.
The finish was the lowest seen since October 30, 1993, when the composite stock index fell to 750.72.

"This was expected," said a Citizens Investment Trust Co fund manager. "Recently, the market had been supported by small-cap shares. It was clear that they wouldn't be able to pull the market up indefinitely."

Concern deepened after Tuesday's release of second quarter GDP figures that showed that the economy had grown at a slower rate this year than last year. GDP grew by a real 6.7 percent in the second quarter against 9.7 percent a year ago.
But news that Hyundai Electronics planned to go public in November hammered the market Wednesday afternoon.
The index fell by 8.41 points, and volume was 19.5 million.
"Hyundai Electronics' listing of shares really impacted the sentiment this afternoon," said Richard Kim of KLB Securities.
Investors believe the market is already suffering from an oversupply of shares. Five firms plan initial public offerings in September, adding 17.55 million more shares to the bourse.
Customer deposits at brokerage houses were at around 2.3 trillion won, while margin loans reached 2.6 trillion. This was adding to the selling pressure, brokers said.
Small-caps and recent risers led the market's tumble. Young Poong Mining fell 2,800 won to 44,700.
